title: CLI + SDK Sample Kits: Distribution, Snippet Packaging, and Canonical Fixes
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary

This playbook defines the canonical format and distribution process for official Redwood SDK + CLI sample kits and embedded docs snippets. It covers: how we package samples for the docs site and NPM/PyPI artifacts, how snippets are linted, tested and rendered in the docs site, and a short canonical-fixes appendix for the top support issues that appear in sample usage. The goal is to reduce support noise, keep examples runnable, and maintain consistent legal/compatibility metadata across channels.

Why this matters

- Many support tickets are caused by out-of-date snippets, missing dependency lines, or inconsistent auth examples between SDKs and the REST API.
- Clear packaging and a small test harness reduces regressions when we change the hosted API or CLI behavior.
- Uniform sample kits improve first-time user success and reduce time-to-value for PLG funnel signups.

Scope and audience

- Audience: Developer experience engineers, SDK maintainers, Docs authors, Solutions engineering.
- Applies to: redwood-cli (rwctl), redwood-js, redwood-py, redwood-go SDKs, and the central docs site renderer.

Kit contents (required per kit)

Each public sample kit MUST contain the following top-level files:

- README.md — short description, prerequisites, and one-line run example.
- LICENSE.txt — MIT (or other approved license) with the standard Redwood attribution header.
- samples/{name}/ — one or more runnable example folders. Each example folder must include:
  - run.md — step-by-step instructions for local execution.
  - env.example — required env vars (REEDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_API_URL, RWCLI_CONFIG).
  - snippet.{lang}.md — the snippet used by docs (see "Snippet packaging" below).
  - tests/quick-run.sh — small smoke test that returns 0 on success.
- package.json / pyproject.toml / go.mod (depending on language) with pinned dev dependencies used by the test harness.
- meta.json — machine readable metadata (minimal, used by release pipeline). Fields required: name, version, sdk_compat (list of semver ranges), tested_with_doc_renderer (true/false), primary_language.

Note: meta.json is a one-line JSON file stored at the kit root. Example content: {"name":"simple-chat","version":"0.2.1","sdk_compat":[">=1.3.0 <2.0.0"],"tested_with_doc_renderer":true,"primary_language":"python"}.

Versioning and compatibility

- SDK version policy: follow semver. Breaking API server changes should be accompanied by SDK minor/major bumps and updated sample kits.
- Each kit must declare sdk_compat ranges for the SDKs it targets. The release pipeline will block publishing a kit if the associated SDK release falls outside that range.

Docs site integration: snippet packaging and rendering

Goals: snippets in docs must be runnable, linted, and display syntax-highlighted code with a consistent copy/paste experience.

Snippet format

- Snippets are stored in each kit as snippet.{lang}.md (e.g., snippet.py.md, snippet.js.md).
- The docs renderer will:
  1) perform placeholder replacement for ENV vars ({{API_KEY_INSTRUCTION}} -> see run.md).
  2) run static linting (black/ruff for Python, eslint for JS) with the style config in repo-root/.snippetrc.
  3) run an execution check in a sandbox (container) for short-lived snippets (<= 20 lines) using the kit's smoke test.

Renderer requirements

- Snippet size limit: 120 lines for display; longer samples link to the repo example folder.
- Output should not contain raw API keys; replace runtime-only values with placeholders.
- Snippets that demonstrate streaming must include both client and server-side behavior (where applicable) and a short note about chunk flush intervals.

Docs-side caching

- Snippet execution results (stdout snapshot) are cached for 7 days.
- Cache invalidation occurs automatically on kit version change or if the meta.json "tested_with_doc_renderer" flips from true to false.

Release checklist for a new kit

1) Author creates kit in samples-repo under samples/<kit-name>/.
2) Fill required files (README.md, env.example, run.md, meta.json, license).
3) Add snippet.{lang}.md files for each language supported.
4) Commit and open PR, include the following PR checklist: smoke tests pass in CI, snippets linting green, meta.json validated.
5) Docs reviewer sign-off (see reviewers list) and release automation tag (kit-release/v*).
6) Automation uploads kit artifact to S3 for docs and to sample-index service for distribution to SDK package installers.

Distribution channels and registry integration

- Docs site: reads kits from s3://redwood-sample-kits/ and uses the meta.json to build the snippet index page.
- NPM/PyPI: For language-specific sample templates we publish a small "redwood-samples" package that references the canonical kits by version. This package must list the kit version in its package metadata to ensure reproducible installs.
- rwctl integration: rwctl sample install <kit-name>@<version> -> downloads kit (checks signature), expands into ~/.rw/samples/<kit-name>/<version>, and runs the kit smoke test.

Security, license and legal requirements

- All shipped kits must include LICENSE.txt and a third-party-deps.md listing external dependencies and their licenses.
- Kits depending on native binaries (FFmpeg, OpenCV) must include an explicit compatibility note in run.md and the tested platform matrix in README.md.

Test harness (technical details)

- Location: infra/snippet-harness/ in monorepo.
- Public API: harness run --kit <path> --test smoke --language python.
- Execution sandbox: uses gVisor + network egress blocked by default. Allowed egress only to REDWOOD_API_TEST_ENDPOINT.
- Output: JSON line: {"kit":"simple-chat","language":"python","status":"pass"} (stored as one-line JSON for CI).

Operational runbooks (docs author flow)

- If a snippet fails linting: authors must fix style in PR. If the fix is nontrivial (requires new dependency), update meta.json and notify SDK maintainers.
- If smoke test fails in CI but passes locally: run the harness in the same image (infra/snippet-harness/docker/dev:latest) and open an infra ticket.
- If smoke test fails due to API contract change: tag the PR with "api-contract-change" and notify the runtime/product team immediately.

Canonical support issues and fixes (top 10)

1) "401 Unauthorized" from SDK examples
- Symptom: examples in README show early 401s for new users.
- Root cause: docs used REDWOOD_API_KEY placeholder but run.md instructs using RW_DEFAULT_KEY. Users copy the wrong var.
- Canonical fix: standardize placeholder to REDWOOD_API_KEY everywhere. Add a one-liner in snippets: # Set env: export REDWOOD_API_KEY"<YOUR_KEY>". Update run.md.

2) Streaming responses hang with Node SDK
- Symptom: fetch() client receives partial chunks and never fires 'end'.
- Root cause: sample uses fetch without setting signal/timeout; server flush interval longer than Node's default read buffer expectation.
- Canonical fix: show streaming snippet using the official redwood-js v1 streaming client and include a small timeout wrapper:

```js
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
const stream = await client.text.generateStream({ model: 'redwood-medium', prompt: 'hi' });
for await (const chunk of stream) { console.log(chunk.text); }
```

3) CORS failures in browser-based snippets
- Symptom: preflight requests blocked when following browser example.
- Root cause: docs used server API URL (internal) instead of browser proxy endpoint.
- Canonical fix: update browser snippets to use the docs-proxy endpoint: https://proxy.docs.redwood.ai/v1 and include instructions in run.md to enable local_dev_proxy in rwctl.

4) Mismatched JSON payloads between REST example and SDK
- Symptom: REST example uses "input_tokens" while SDK uses "input" (legacy field drift).
- Root cause: historical rename not reflected in some older kits.
- Canonical fix: unify on the server-stable field names in samples, add a small compatibility note: "If you maintain older kits, include a compatibility adapter snippet" with a short python example:

```py
def adapt_payload(payload):
    if 'input_tokens' in payload:
        payload['input'] = payload.pop('input_tokens')
    return payload
```

5) Windows CRLF / shebang problems for shell scripts
- Symptom: smoke tests fail for scripts with CRLF; shebang lines not recognized in Git Bash.
- Canonical fix: normalize scripts in CI with dos2unix and include a note in CONTRIBUTING.md. Provide .gitattributes with text eol=lf for scripts.

6) rwctl sample install fails with certificate error in corporate proxies
- Symptom: curl/requests fail with TLS verify error during kit download.
- Canonical fix: document proxy env vars (HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY, NO_PROXY) in run.md and add a rwctl flag --insecure-for-proxy-debug that emits safe debugging hints (not for production). Create support KB entry with commands to validate proxy chain.

7) Snippet linter version mismatch
- Symptom: CI fails with different linting results than local dev machines.
- Canonical fix: pin snippet linter versions in kit package files and provide a dev container (/.devcontainer) with exact versions. Update CI to build from the same devcontainer image.

8) Cross-language example drift (Python vs JS)
- Symptom: example outputs are subtly different because of default temperature or max_tokens mismatch.
- Canonical fix: explicitly set generation config in every example and include a "golden_output.txt" in the example folder for regression testing. E.g., 

```py
resp = client.text.generate(model='redwood-medium', prompt='Say hi', temperature=0.0, max_tokens=16)
```

9) Sample uses heavy model by default causing quota/latency issues
- Symptom: new users run example and exceed free-tier quota quickly.
- Canonical fix: default to the lightweight model alias (redwood-light) in samples and add a short note: "Switch to redwood-medium for higher quality at increased cost."

10) Missing third-party dependency on CI images (libGL, ffmpeg)
- Symptom: code that uses image processing fails in harness because CI image lacks required system libs.
- Canonical fix: list system deps in README and add them to dockerfiles used for the harness. Add a postinstall check script that early-fails with a friendly message.

Owner and escalation

- Kit author: initial owner until the kit is promoted to a maintained kit.
- Maintainer (long-term): assign an SDK owner in OWNERS file under the kit directory.
- Escalation path: docs author -> eng-devex (pager) -> infra (snippet-harness oncall) -> runtime/product for API breaks.

Metrics to monitor

- % of published snippets passing harness smoke tests (target: 99%).
- Mean time between snippet-related support tickets (target: reduce by 50% in 6 months).
- RWCTL sample install success rate per region (target: 99.5%).

Appendix: example snippet (Python minimal)

```py
from redwood import RedwoodClient
import os

client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY'])
resp = client.text.generate(model='redwood-light', prompt='Translate to French: Hello')
print(resp.text)
```

Appendix: example rwctl usage

1) Install kit

$ rwctl sample install simple-chat@0.2.1

2) Run smoke test

$ ~/.rw/samples/simple-chat/0.2.1/tests/quick-run.sh
